get.summary: Confirm email change with verification code
get.description: Completes the email change process using the verification code sent to the new email address.

post.summary: Request to change the email address for the authenticated user
post.description:
Initiates an email change process by sending a verification code to the new email address.
The user must click the confirmation link in the email to complete the change.

get.summary: Public OTP-login enablement flag for a Realm.
get.description:
Reads the `email_otp` / `settings` config row. Returns `{ enabled: false }`
when the config is absent or malformed (opt-in per Realm).

post.summary: Authenticate user with email/username and password
post.description:
Supports both email and username login. Returns a session token or requires TOTP verification
if two-factor authentication is enabled for the user.

post.summary: Send an email OTP login code.
post.description:
Issues a one-time verification code for an existing active user, or — if the
Realm has OTP auto-register enabled — for an unregistered email after consent
is expressed. Enumeration-resistant: a 200 is returned for non-active or
non-existent users (no code sent in those cases), matching the response for
a successful send.

400.description: OTP login not enabled for realm / bad request

401.description: Client App disabled / Turnstile verification failed

409.description: Consent required (auto-register) or email not registered (auto-register off)

post.summary: Verify an email OTP login code and issue a session.
post.description:
On a matching code: consumes it (one-time), then either logs the existing
user in (login-as-consent gate) or auto-registers a new account
(create-without-password → activate → register-as-consent) and issues a
Bearer token family via `RedisBrowserTokenService`. Returns `BrowserTokenResponse`.

400.description: OTP login not enabled for realm / bad request

401.description: Invalid / expired / exhausted code, or disabled account

404.description: Passkey is not enabled for this realm

post.summary: Verify TOTP code for two-factor authentication
post.description:
Completes the login process for users with TOTP enabled. Accepts either a TOTP code
from an authenticator app or a backup code. Creates a permanent session on success.

401.description: Invalid TOTP code or backup code

post.description:
Creates a new user account with email and optional username. If email verification is required
for realm, account will be created in a pending state and a verification email will be sent.

post.summary: Confirm password reset with verification code
post.description: Completes password reset process using verification code sent to user's email.

302.description: Password reset successful; redirecting to the registered Client App URL.

post.description:
Initiates a password reset process by sending a verification code to user's email address.
Always returns success to prevent email enumeration.

get.summary: Get Turnstile configuration status for a Client App
get.description:
Returns whether Turnstile verification is enabled for the specified Client
App and the site key to render the widget. Turnstile is fully delegated to
the Client App (D-PROTECT-01); the legacy realm_config source is no longer
read. A missing or disabled Client App is rejected with 401, matching the
other anonymous Client-App-bound endpoints. Pass `clientId` as a query
parameter.

401.description: Client app not found or disabled

get.description:
Completes email verification process using verification code sent to user's email.
Activates user account upon successful verification.

302.description: Email verified; redirecting to the registered Client App URL.

post.description:
Sends a verification email to specified email address with a confirmation link.
Used to initiate email verification for pending accounts.

Verifies an Apple `identityToken` (from `ASAuthorizationAppleIDProvider`)
server-side and, depending on `downstreamState`, issues either a direct
browser session (Bearer token family bound to `clientId`) or a downstream
authorization code for the Code+PKCE flow. Requires the realm to have an
enabled Apple provider.

200.description: Downstream-authorization-code mode: redirect URI returned for Code+PKCE exchange

400.description: Bad request (validation error or missing/invalid downstream state)

404.description: Apple provider not configured or not enabled

post.description:
Verifies a Google One Tap (GIS) ID Token server-side and, depending on
`downstreamState`, issues either a direct browser session (Bearer token
family bound to `clientId`) or a downstream authorization code for the
Code+PKCE flow. Requires the realm to have an enabled Google provider.

200.description: Downstream-authorization-code mode: redirect URI returned for Code+PKCE exchange

400.description: Bad request (validation error or missing/invalid downstream state)

401.description: Unauthorized (ID Token signature/issuer/audience/expiry validation failed, or email not verified)

404.description: Google provider not configured or not enabled

get.summary: Get public configuration for a realm
get.description:
Returns publicly accessible configuration for the specified realm, including:
- Registration settings (whether registration is allowed and if email verification is required)
- List of enabled OAuth providers
- Published white-label settings

This endpoint does not require authentication.

EmailOtpConflictResponse.description:
Shared body for both 409 branches. `consent_required` carries the current
effective agreement summaries + `consent_required=true`; `email_not_registered`
carries a guidance message and no agreements.

LegalAgreementSummary.description:
Public agreement list item (no `content` body). Shared by the public
agreements endpoint and the login `consent_required` branch.

`agreement_type` is a raw `String` here (not the enum) so this DTO doubles
as an OpenAPI-facing shape consumed by `herald-api` / `herald-api-auth`
without forcing those callers to depend on the enum's serde representation.

permissions.description:
Retained in the response shape for clients that display RBAC grants;
browser-token authorization itself is governed by `scopes`.

redirectUri.description:
Full redirect URI returned by `issue_downstream_authorization_code`,
including `?code=ac_...&state=...` for the downstream Code+PKCE flow.

clientId.description: Herald ClientApp `client_id` that the direct-session token family binds to.

downstreamState.description:
Optional downstream authorization transaction identifier (OAuth `state`).
Presence selects the downstream-authorization-code branch; absence the
direct-session branch.

clientId.description: Herald ClientApp `client_id` that the direct-session token family binds to.

credential.description: Google One Tap issued ID Token (JWT), from the GIS `credential` callback.

downstreamState.description:
Optional downstream authorization transaction identifier (OAuth `state`).
Presence selects the downstream-authorization-code branch; absence the
direct-session branch.

clientId.description:
Provider `client_id` (e.g. Google One Tap / GIS initialization). Not a
secret — the redirect-style `/login` flow already surfaces it in the
auth URL. `client_secret` is never exposed here. Omitted from the
serialized payload when absent to keep the response stable for existing
consumers that only read `name`/`displayName`/`enabled`.

Full redirect URI returned by `issue_downstream_authorization_code`,
including `?code=ac_...&state=...` for the downstream Code+PKCE flow.
